I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Using the same rules, my script reproduces all 10 of your Q2 reference values exactly.

```json
{"a_segment": "smb", "a_net": 304620605, "b_customers": 249, "c_category": "svc", "c_net": 269600568, "d_month": "2025-09", "e_email": "u16@ex.com", "f_repeat": 231, "g_avg": 668212, "h_growth": 11.4}
```

Your definitions were applied as written, but matching the Q2 values took three choices about the data:

- **Dates are in Korean time:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (it ends in `Z`). I added 9 hours to get Korean time (KST) before assigning orders to the quarter and to a month. Without this, 7 of the 10 Q2 values come out wrong.
- **A customer is an email address:** 300 customer IDs share only 250 emails, so some people have more than one ID. Counting customers by email is what reproduces b (228) and f (187). Counting by ID gives 270 and 210.
- **Segment names are cleaned up:** the segment field has variants like `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '` and `'SMB'`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.

Every order is counted once, under the segment of the customer ID that placed it. h compares August (2nd month) with September (3rd month).

The script is at `/tmp/an/calc.py`.
